## Purpose

An "entry" module is a standalone `run <name>` command: a public `*Opts` struct capturing its CLI arguments, and a `pub fn run(opts: ...Opts)` (or nested `run`) that performs the whole operation and prints its own byte-stable output. `git_settle.rs`, `maint/claude_dir_prune.rs`, and `maint/rehook.rs` are each self-contained — they own their report/entry types locally and do not leak internals to siblings, only importing shared low-level helpers (`shared::context::project_dir`, `mustard_core::ClaudePaths`).

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 14

Every exemplar opens with a module doc-comment naming the exact `mustard-rt run <name>` invocation and stating its fail-open contract up front ("Exit code 0 always", "Fail-open: ... each surface as their own `state` string rather than erroring"). Options are a plain `pub struct FooOpts { ... }` (no builder), and per-item results are small `Serialize` structs (`RestoredEntry`, one entry per classified path) collected into a report struct rendered as pretty JSON.

## How to apply

Name the file after the command's snake_case name (`claude_dir_prune.rs` for `claude-dir-prune`). Register it via the two-registration rule (variant in the family's `*Cmd` enum + arm in `dispatch()`) per the crate CLAUDE.md guard. Keep classification/audit tables as module-level `const` slices (`KEEP_DIRS`, `LEGACY_DIRS`) rather than inline literals, and document any single-source-of-truth relationship (e.g. `documented_dirs()` deriving from `ClaudePaths::documented_dirs`).

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/maint/rehook.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/commands/maint/claude_dir_prune.rs

```rust
/// Options for `mustard-rt run rehook`.
pub struct RehookOpts {
    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub scope: String,
    pub confirm: bool,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct RestoredEntry {
    pub settings_path: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub restored_from: Option<String>,
    pub state: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub error: Option<String>,
}
```
